label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

findings.problem: Country pop-up: focus is not placed on it and nothing is focused when it opens, I had to tab to find the two links
Skip to main content link lands on a promo banner link and an unnamed link before real content; skipping does not move focus reliably, afterwards nothing is focused
Product card links have a vague name like 8 colors instead of the product name, and each card has an extra Next image button before it, so finding a product takes many tabs after 4 filter buttons
Five focusable unnamed divs from the image gallery come before the product options, and a survey radio group (Not At All Likely) stole focus out of order and would not dismiss cleanly
Fit options Regular Tall Petite are checkboxes not radios, and the colour radio has no name; stock only said In stock after choosing a size, with no announcement
After Add to Bag the confirmation appeared but focus stayed on the Add to Bag button behind it, so I needed two more tabs to find Checkout

Bag page shows developer text saying a placeholder div should not be displayed, and the Skip to shopping bag link only focuses the header bag icon, not the bag contents; reaching Checkout needs about 40 tabs through nav, promo banners, unnamed links and a nine-item Best Sellers carousel, so I ran out of steps before the payment step
